title: Iron ore and development in Orissa
body: Orissa holds some of the largest untapped iron ore reserves in the country, and the global demand for steel is rising. The State government has signed Memoranda of Understanding with international and domestic steel makers, hoping the projects will bring capital investment and many jobs. The ore, however, lies in some of the most underdeveloped and mainly tribal districts of the State. Tribal communities fear that the industries will displace them from their homes and livelihoods, and some villagers have protested outside a steel company's office demanding that its agreement be cancelled. Environmentalists fear that mining and industry will pollute the environment. The central government feels that refusing the industry would set a bad example and discourage investment in the country.

title: The push for heavy industry
body: The Second Five Year Plan, drafted by a team led by P.C. Mahalanobis, sought quick structural transformation of the economy. Substantial tariffs on imports protected domestic industries, and key industries such as electricity, railways, steel, machinery and communication were developed in the public sector. The strategy had its problems. India was technologically backward and had to spend scarce foreign exchange on technology from abroad, and because industry attracted more investment than agriculture, the danger of food shortage grew. Some critics said the plans showed an 'urban bias'; others said industry was wrongly placed before agriculture; still others wanted the focus to be on agriculture-related industries rather than heavy ones.
